title: MatterGen proposes TaCr2O6; researchers synthesize it and estimate a bulk modulus of 169 GPa against a 200 GPa target
summary: Researchers synthesized MatterGen’s proposed TaCr2O6 and estimated its bulk modulus at 169 GPa from indentation measurements, below the 200 GPa design target.
account: Zeni et al. reported MatterGen in Nature on January 16,2025. The diffusion model was trained on 607,683 stable crystal structures. For experimental validation, successive filters reduced generated candidates to 75 and experts selected four for synthesis. One produced TaCr2O6 with compositional disorder between Ta and Cr. Researchers measured Young’s modulus by nanoindentation and estimated bulk modulus using a DFT-computed Poisson ratio of 0.30. Four estimates yielded 158±11 GPa; the authors chose the maximum,169 GPa, as their best estimate for a potentially noncompact powder sample, against a 200 GPatarget. The synthesis and measurement belong to the vendor-coauthored study; independent experimental replication is not established.
purpose: Generate novel stable inorganic materials conditioned on target properties
deployer: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences (synthesis)
taxonomy_note: A generated and synthesized compound is a research result rather than access to existing information.

ratings.reason: A single proof-of-concept synthesis by the paper's co-authors.

ai_role.statement: MatterGen generated candidates that researchers filtered and selected for synthesis. One of four selected candidates yielded disordered TaCr2O6. Researchers estimated its bulk modulus from nanoindentation measurements and a computed Poisson ratio; the reported 169 GPa was the maximum of four estimates. The developer-coauthored study does not establish independent replication or commercial usefulness.

evidence.citation: Zeni C, Pinsler R, Zugner D, et al. Nature 639:624-632 (2025)
evidence.title: A generative model for inorganic materials design
evidence.quote: As a proof of concept, we synthesize one of the generated structures and measure its property value to be within 20% of our target.

evidence.title: MatterGen: A new paradigm of materials design with generative AI
evidence.quote: The synthesized material's structure aligns with the one proposed by MatterGen, with the caveat of compositional disorder between Ta and Cr.

produced_by: Diffusion model fine-tuned on a bulk-modulus target
Synthesis and measurement by a collaborating laboratory
must_hold: Confirmation that generated compounds are new rather than known phases

headline: MatterGen proposes a material with an estimated 169 GPa bulk modulus
metric: Estimated bulk modulus of 169 GPa; target 200 GPa

comparator.against: previous generative models for crystal structures (DiffCSP, CDVAE and others) on the same benchmark
comparator.before: not stated as a figure in the text (previous generative models)
comparator.after: more than twice as likely to be SUN (stable, unique and new); the synthesized TaCr2O6 measured at 169 GPa against a 200 GPa design target
comparator.quote: Combining both model and data improvements, MatterGen generates structures that are more than twice as likely to be SUN compared with previous generative models, whereas the generated structures are up to an order of magnitude closer to their local energy minimum.

later.note: A Materials Horizons paper by Mikkel Juelsholt (12 June 2026) reports that the synthesized disordered TaCr2O6 is identical to Ta1/2Cr1/2O2, a compound first described in 1971 and included in MatterGen's training dataset, so the proof-of-concept material was not new.
later.quote: However, detailed crystallographic analysis presented in this paper reveals that this is not a novel compound but is identical to the previously reported Ta1/2Cr1/2O2, first described in 1971 and included in MatterGen's training dataset.

fields.account: Zeni et al. reported MatterGen in Nature on January 16,2025. The diffusion model was trained on 607,683 stable crystal structures. For experimental validation, successive filters reduced generated candidates to 75 and experts selected four for synthesis. One produced TaCr2O6 with compositional disorder between Ta and Cr. Researchers measured Young’s modulus by nanoindentation and estimated bulk modulus using a DFT-computed Poisson ratio of 0.30. Four estimates yielded 158±11 GPa; the authors chose the maximum,169 GPa, as their best estimate for a potentially noncompact powder sample, against a 200 GPatarget. The synthesis and measurement belong to the vendor-coauthored study; independent experimental replication is not established.
